relevance_reason: This paper reports an NBAS truncating mutation in a family with acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis, which is the subject of this entry, and includes functional and animal-model evidence.

findings.statement: Palagano et al. (2018) studied an Indian family with 2 affected sibs diagnosed with acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis type 1. They described it as an extremely rare autosomal recessive syndrome with facial and skeletal abnormalities, short stature, and intellectual disability.
quotes: Acrofrontofacionasal Dysostosis type 1 (AFFND1) is an extremely rare, autosomal recessive syndrome, comprising facial and skeletal abnormalities, short stature and intellectual disability.
We analyzed an Indian family with two affected siblings

findings.statement: In 2 affected sibs from an Indian family with acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis, Palagano et al. (2018) used exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the NBAS gene. Overexpressing the truncated NBAS protein in HEK293T cells impaired both nonsense-mediated decay and Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde traffic.
quotes: identified a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the Neuroblastoma-Amplified Sequence (NBAS) gene in the patients' genome
Both functions were impaired in HEK293T cells overexpressing the truncated NBAS protein, as assessed by Real-Time PCR, Western blot analysis, co-immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence analysis.

findings.statement: Palagano et al. (2018) found by immunohistochemistry that NBAS protein was expressed in mouse embryos. Expression was seen in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic skeletal structures and in the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum. In zebrafish embryos, depleting endogenous z-nbas caused defective morphogenesis of chondrogenic cranial skeletal elements.
quotes: detected expression in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic structures of the skeleton as well as in the cortex, hippocampus and cerebellum, which is compatible with a role in bone and brain development
depletion of endogenous z-nbas in fish embryos results in defective morphogenesis of chondrogenic cranial skeletal elements
